name: 32774-loramoe-qwen3moe30b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of an a3 node
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1; `fully_sharded_loras` left at its default (off)
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=80, bounded at 800 requests with a 1800 s safety cap, warmup the first 10% and cooldown the last 10% by completion.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix buckets, no tools: fixed-shape random-token requests, 1024 prompt tokens and exactly 100 output tokens, both pinned min=max and enforced with `max_tokens` + `ignore_eos`. `request_format: plain` sends the sampled tokens with no chat template, so the wire prompt is exactly 1024. Greedy (temperature 0.0). Every request carries an adapter, alternating over the two declared names.
purpose: A domain-specialist assistant on a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, two LoRA adapters, 80 concurrent 1024-token prompts, single GPU.
launch:
# The engine's arguments. Every key goes straight into AsyncEngineArgs.
model: Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# LoRA serving IS the setup: two adapter slots resident, every request carrying an adapter. The
# adapter names are declared client-side in scenario.json, because `--lora-modules` is an
# API-server argument and this engine is built in-process.
enable-lora: true
max-loras: 2
# Follows the adapter actually loaded (adapter_config.json: r=8): max_lora_rank sizes the stacked
# LoRA buffers, so a larger value here just pads them with zeros.
max-lora-rank: 8

# Off: the prompts come from a random-token generator with no shared prefix, and the default here
# would be ON, so a chance block hit between two synthetic prompts would remove prefill work.
enable-prefix-caching: false

# Written out, not left to resolve: the in-process engine path (UsageContext.ENGINE_CONTEXT) is in
# neither per-context default table and falls through to 2048 / 128, a quarter of the prefill
# budget an API server would get.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024

# The workload's worst case is 1024 + 100 = 1124 tokens; left alone the engine would take the
# checkpoint's 40960, which only inflates the block tables.
max-model-len: 2048

# Above the engine's 0.90 default because ~57 GiB of weights is large relative to the card; this
# leaves ~14 GiB of KV, comfortably more than the 80 x 1124-token working set needs.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.93

# Read off the checkpoint's config.json, pinned so a future default cannot drift it.
dtype: bfloat16
